title: The Perfect Serve (Bar)
blurb: Clean correct glassware, a proper pour, correct measures and finishing touches so every drink is the same excellent standard.
siteNotes: The venue's standard glass and garnish for each drink (the drinks spec)
Which spirit and wine measures the venue uses, and where the measures are displayed
How cask ales are kept and how long they settle before serving
Who to tell about a cloudy beer or a possible line or cellar fault
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-27. Good bar practice, plus the legal point on measures: Weights and Measures Act 1985 and the orders made under it, and the licensing requirement to display measures.

CHECK: the trainer says measuring spirits correctly is a legal requirement. It is for spirits sold by the measure (the measure sizes sold must be displayed and prescribed quantities used for some spirits), but not every drink or every cocktail is covered. Confirm the venue's measures and notices, and that wine is offered in the required sizes.
CHECK: the trainer treats a chipped glass as a safety issue to be binned. Confirm the venue's broken and chipped glass procedure matches.

cards.title: The Perfect Serve (Bar)
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- choose and check the right glass
- pour, measure and serve to standard
- finish every drink to spec

cards.title: Consistency is everything
cards.body: A guest who gets a beautifully poured pint or a properly made G&T on the first visit expects exactly the same on the tenth. Deliver it every time and that is how we build a reputation and a loyal crowd. The perfect serve is just doing the simple things right, drink after drink.

cards.title: Right glass, clean, unchipped
cards.body:
Use the correct, clean glassware for each drink, chilled where it should be. Check it is spotless and unchipped before you pour.
> A chipped glass is a safety issue. Bin it.

cards.title: Beer, spirits and wine

items.title: Draught beer
items.text: Serve to a proper head; let cask ale settle if it needs it

items.title: Check the beer
items.text: Clear and bright. Cloudy or off beer means a line or cellar issue to flag

items.title: Spirits
items.text: The right measure every time: a legal requirement and good practice

cards.title: Finish to spec
cards.body: Garnish and finish drinks to spec every single time. It only takes a few extra seconds, and it is the difference between a drink that is just wet and one a guest is pleased to be handed.

items.title: Garnish
items.text: The correct one for the drink

items.title: Clean pour
items.text: Down the side of the glass

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Consistency drink after drink builds our reputation.
- Clean, correct, unchipped glass. Bin chipped glass.
- Draught to a proper head, cask settled, beer clear and bright. Flag cloudy beer.
- Correct measures every time. Wine at the right temperature and measure.
- Garnish, ice and pour to spec. It only takes a few seconds.

cards.q: On the bar, consistency drink-to-drink is what builds our reputation.
cards.why: A guest expects the tenth visit to match the first, so consistency is what builds a loyal crowd.

options: Any glass to hand
Full already
Clean, correct and unchipped
Warm from the glasswasher
cards.why: Use the correct, clean glassware and check it is spotless and unchipped before you pour.

cards.q: What should you do with a chipped glass?
options: Use it for drinks served over ice
Keep it aside for staff drinks
Put it through the glasswasher as normal
Bin it
cards.why: A chipped glass is a safety issue and has to be binned.

cards.q: Cloudy or "off" beer usually means a line or cellar issue to flag.
cards.why: Check the beer looks clear and bright before it goes out. If not, flag a likely line or cellar issue.

cards.q: Spirits must be measured with the correct measure because…
options: It makes the drink look nicer
It is optional for house spirits
It is a legal requirement and good practice
The guest might ask to see it
cards.why: Measuring spirits correctly is a legal requirement as well as good practice.

cards.q: The type of glass can affect how a drink looks, smells and tastes.
cards.why: The right glass is not fussiness. It genuinely affects how a drink looks, smells and tastes.

cards.q: Which is part of presentation for the perfect serve?
options: Pouring as fast as you can
Using whichever glass is nearest
The correct garnish for the drink
Leaving the ice until last
cards.why: Garnish and finish drinks to spec: the correct garnish, the right ice and a clean pour down the side of the glass.

cards.q: Cask ale may need to settle before serving.
cards.why: Let cask ales settle if they need it.

options: At whatever temperature it is
Always as cold as possible
At the right temperature and measure
Straight off the shelf, room-warm
cards.why: Serve wine at the right temperature and measure.

cards.q: Doing the perfect serve properly only takes a few extra seconds.
cards.why: It only takes a few extra seconds and it is the difference between a drink that is just wet and one a guest is pleased to be handed.
